title: Breadboard Connection Explorer
creator: Hank R. & Claude Code
subject: Environmental Monitoring
description: Click any hole to light up every hole joined to it, reveal the hidden copper strips underneath, and then find the one wrong connection in three pre-wired circuits.

learningObjectives: Explain which holes on a breadboard are electrically connected to one another.
Predict whether two components placed in given holes will form a working circuit.
prerequisites: Chapter 3 sections on circuits and the complete loop
The Circuit Loop and the Missing Ground MicroSim

keyQuestions: Why is there a channel down the middle of the board?
A chip works fine on the bench but not on the breadboard. What would you check first?
Are the upper and lower positive rails connected to each other?
commonMisconceptions: Assuming a whole numbered column is one strip, when the channel splits it in two.
Assuming the two power rails on opposite edges are joined.
Thinking adjacent columns are connected because the holes are close together.
assessmentOpportunities: States which holes on a breadboard are electrically joined, without looking it up.
Explains the purpose of the centre channel in terms of chips straddling it.
Finds a wiring fault from a described symptom rather than by trial and error.
